title: Russia strikes Dnipro with an Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile
body:
On 21 November 2024 Russian President Vladimir Putin said in a televised address that Russian forces had struck a defence industry facility in Dnipro, central Ukraine, with a new missile called Oreshnik. He described it as a medium-range ballistic missile with a non-nuclear hypersonic warhead. Novaya Gazeta Europe reported his remarks the same day.

Earlier that day Ukraine's Air Force had reported that Russia launched an intercontinental ballistic missile at Dnipro. A US official later told Reuters that the missile was medium-range, not an intercontinental one.

Putin said the strike was a response to Ukrainian attacks on Bryansk and Kursk with US- and UK-made missiles. He said that no existing missile defence systems, including those in Europe, could intercept Oreshnik-type missiles, and that Russia would decide on further deployment of medium- and shorter-range missiles based on the actions of the United States and its allies. He added that Russia would warn Ukrainian civilians to leave danger zones if it targeted other facilities with ballistic missiles. The article did not report the extent of damage or casualties.
